open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict lookup when the corpus grows
open_points.text: “when an implementation is submitted and no verdict for it and the current corpus digest exists” does not say whether “for it” means for the implementation alone or for the implementation–corpus-digest pair; this conflicts with “a grown corpus needs a new verdict” under the implementation-only reading
open_points.question: When an implementation already has a verdict for an earlier corpus digest and is submitted against a grown corpus, must the kernel compute and record a new verdict for the new implementation–corpus pair?
options: Look up by implementation_id plus current corpus_digest; compute a new verdict when that pair is absent.
Look up by implementation_id alone; once any verdict exists for the implementation, never compute another.
open_points.default_guess: Look up by the implementation_id and current corpus_digest pair.

witness.initial: Implementation I has an admitted verdict for corpus digest C1.
events: An author adds a trial case, growing the contract version's corpus to digest C2.
An agent submits the same implementation I again.
outcomes: The kernel finds no verdict for pair (I, C2), runs every case in C2, records a new verdict, and activates I if admitted.
The kernel finds that I already has a verdict, runs no admission, and cannot provide the current-corpus verdict required for activation.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and anyone inspecting the contract version's activation and admission evidence.
